newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian troops deployed on Madura after riots.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian troops deployed on Madura after riots.

text.p: Indonesia has deployed at least 3,000 troops on Madura island off eastern Java after riots sparked by the ruling Golkar party's sweep of general elections, police said on Monday.
Angry Moslems started rioting following the elections on Thursday and violence continued through the weekend.
Golkar took more than 74 percent of the national vote, with the Moslem-backed United Development Party (PPP) winning almost 23 percent.
The only other party permitted to contest the poll, the badly fragmented Christian-Nationalist Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI), slumped to three percent.

A re-vote is to be held at two locations on Madura after ballot boxes were destroyed on Thursday night. The island is a PPP stronghold. "We have deployed around 3,000 troops on the island to counter violence, especially because there will be a re-vote on Tuesday," East Java police spokesman Lieutenant-Colonel Sofwat Hadi told Reuters by telephone.
"We will take stern action against rioters. There will be no compromise," said Hadi, adding that Madura was generally calm on Monday.

In other election turmoil, at least 34 people, including 16 policemen and two soldiers, were killed in East Timor over a four-day period in violence related to separatist attempts to disrupt the polls in the former Portuguese colony and a Saturday morning ambush of an election protection unit, police reported.
The official Antara news agency said on Monday the General Election Committee would reopen polling stations in Sampang and Pamekasan towns on Madura for the re-vote there.
Thousands of people rioted on Thursday night, burning houses, offices and a church, alleging vote rigging after Golkar appeared to be sweeping the election on Madura.
Violence continued early on Sunday when unidentified people set fire to houses and government offices in the town of Pamekasan, Antara said. In Sumenep, three government offices were burned, it said.
Hadi confirmed the report and said police were still questioning nine people after Thursday's violence. He gave no further details.

Golkar chairman Harmoko on Sunday rejected claims that there were systematic violations of electoral laws and vote rigging in favour of Golkar, as charged by an independent election watchdog set up by activists and government critics.
The PPP also said there had been election irregularities and that it would meet this week to decide whether to accept the result.
Golkar won 68 percent of votes in the last election in 1992, the PPP 17 percent and the PDI 15 percent.
